The outlined treatment plan for Grace’s osteoarthritis is highly appropriate and aligns with standard clinical guidelines for managing this condition. Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease characterized by the breakdown of cartilage, leading to pain and stiffness. The recommended interventions address the core aspects of management: pain control, mechanical support, and functional improvement.

Taking over-the-counter pain relievers (such as acetaminophen or NSAIDs) is a first-line approach for mild to moderate pain, helping to manage symptoms without the risks associated with stronger prescription medications. Low-impact aerobic exercises like swimming and biking are ideal because they maintain cardiovascular health and joint mobility without placing excessive stress on the knee joints, which high-impact activities might exacerbate. Furthermore, physical therapy focused on strengthening the muscles around the knees (particularly the quadriceps and hamstrings) is crucial. Stronger muscles provide better support and stability to the joint, reducing the load on the cartilage and potentially slowing disease progression. This multimodal approach is widely recognized as effective in reducing pain, improving function, and enhancing quality of life for patients with knee osteoarthritis.
